text:
monitor-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — SLA breach detected for tenant KioskCorp on service `kiosk-embed-prod`
- symptom: 5xx spike & 95th latency > 2.1s for embeddings API (tenant check)
- affected routes: /v1/embeddings (tenant_id=kioskcorp)
- first_seen: 2026-03-15T10:14:14Z
- current_count(5m): errors=342, p95=2.12s
link: https://console.redwood.example/alerts/1968007654

maya: oncall — acked. jumping in. any recent deploys for kiosk-embed-prod?

sam: not that I know of, no rollout in last 24h. looks like a traffic surge from KioskCorp's batch job. saw repeated `ERR_MODEL_TIMEOUT` in logs.

maya: copying logs now, attaching short tail.
```
kiosk-embed-pod-7f9c container logs: 
[10:12:34] request tenant=kioskcorp id=abc123 latency=2100ms err=ERR_MODEL_TIMEOUT
[10:12:34] request tenant=kioskcorp id=abc124 latency=2120ms err=ERR_MODEL_TIMEOUT
[10:12:35] request tenant=kioskcorp id=abc125 latency=2050ms err=ERR_MODEL_TIMEOUT
```

sam: that pattern suggests model queueing + timeouts. tenant is hitting large concurrent embedding batches. p50 still ok for other tenants. this is tenant-scoped.

diego: recommend immediate mitigations: 1) silence the noisy tenant-level SLA alerts for 30m to stop repeated pages, 2) add a short-term route limit or soft-cap for kioskcorp, 3) scale up dedicated pool for embedding workers if we have spare capacity.

maya: doing silence now: `redwood-silence add --tenant kioskcorp --duration 30m --reason "active mitigation"` (will post confirmation).

oncall-bot: Silence created: kioskcorp, 30m — ID s-20260315-01 — created by maya. :white_check_mark:

leo: I'll create a temporary throttling policy on the gateway to cap concurrency to 40 for kioskcorp while we investigate. applying in prod in 2m.

sam: also adding a dedup rule to monitoring: if identical tenant check fires >5 times in 5m, treat as single incident and escalate based on unique error class, not raw count. will push a rule change. snippet: 
```
- alert: TenantEmbeddingErrors
  expr: sum by (tenant, err_class) (increase(embedding_errors_total[5m])) > 5
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    runbook: https://confluence.redwood.example/runbooks/tenant-embed
```

maya: attempting a rolling restart of `kiosk-embed-prod` pods after throttle in case some pods are in a bad state: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/kiosk-embed-prod -n inference`

sam: confirmed several pods were saturated. scaling replica count from 6 -> 10 as a short-term bump: `kubectl scale deployment/kiosk-embed-prod --replicas=10 -n inference`. Watch CPU/queue metrics.

leo: throttle policy applied at edge; rate observed dropping ~60% for kioskcorp. dashboard will reflect in a few mins.

diego: filing follow-up actions: create a dashboard tile for tenant concurrency, add per-tenant p95 alert, and add a tenant-level SLA suppression mechanism to our on-call runbook. assigning to maya for runbook update and to leo for grafana tile. ticket: RWF-1567 created.

maya: adding note to incident log: temporary mutex discovered in embedding worker under high-concurrency for specific model variant. will schedule deeper root cause with infra/ML.

oncall-bot: pager history: 5 pages, 3 silenced, responders: maya, sam, leo. Handoff ETA: next oncall at 10:40 UTC.

sam: monitoring shows error rate trending down. p95 back to 1.1s for kioskcorp after throttle + scale.

monitor-bot: RESOLVED — alert for 1968007654 cleared at 2026-03-15T10:17:55Z. Incident classified as "tenant over-concurrency causing transient model timeouts".

maya: summary for postmortem: cause=tenant batch concurrency + model worker queueing; mitigation=throttle tenant + scale pods + restart pods; followups=add per-tenant dashboard, add dedup/aggregation rule for tenant alerts, add runbook entry + schedule model-level perf testing under tenant-like concurrency. assigning owners: dashboard=leo, runbook=maya, RCA=sam/diego.

diego: leaving reminder: add a non-alerting anomaly detector for tenant spike patterns so we can auto-suggest burst-capacity instead of paging.

maya: thanks all — documenting PRs/tickets now. :thumbsup:
